items.title: Egypt Traffic Fines and Violations Guide
items.content_text: Traffic fines in Egypt are issued electronically through smart cameras and traffic police, with penalties ranging from small fees to vehicle impoundment.

items.title: Egypt Electricity and Utility Bills: A Practical Guide
items.content_text: Electricity, water, and gas in Egypt are billed by state-run utility companies, with electricity priced on a tiered scale based on monthly consumption.

items.title: Food Allergies vs Food Intolerances: What's the Difference
items.content_text: A food allergy involves the immune system and can be life-threatening, while a food intolerance is a digestive issue that causes discomfort but isn't dangerous.

items.title: The History of the Prophet's Mosque in Medina
items.content_text: The Prophet's Mosque in Medina was built in 622 CE by Prophet Muhammad himself and has grown from a simple structure into one of Islam's holiest sites.

items.title: How Al-Azhar's Islamic Education System Works
items.content_text: Al-Azhar operates a parallel education track in Egypt, from primary school through university, combining religious and modern academic subjects.

items.title: How Do APIs Work? The Bridge That Lets Apps Talk
items.content_text: An API is a defined set of rules that lets one piece of software request data or functions from another, acting as a structured bridge between programs.

items.title: How Do Volcanoes Actually Erupt?
items.content_text: Volcanic eruptions happen when molten rock, gas, and pressure inside the Earth build up until they force their way through a weak point in the crust.

items.title: How Gold Prices Are Determined Globally
items.content_text: Gold's global price is set through continuous trading on international markets, driven by central bank demand, the US dollar, and investor sentiment.

items.title: How Import Tariffs Actually Work
items.content_text: An import tariff is a tax a government charges on goods entering the country, usually collected from the importer at customs before goods are released.

items.title: How National Lottery Draws Actually Work
items.content_text: Lottery draws use certified random number generators or physical ball machines, with independent auditors and public draws designed to prove fairness.

items.title: The Legend of Anansi the Spider
items.content_text: Anansi is a clever trickster spider from West African folklore who outwits stronger characters through wit rather than strength, and became a Caribbean folk hero too.

items.title: The Legend of Beowulf
items.content_text: Beowulf is an Old English epic poem about a hero who defeats the monster Grendel, and it's one of the oldest surviving works of English literature.

items.title: The Legend of the Kraken
items.content_text: The Kraken is a legendary sea monster from Scandinavian folklore, said to be large enough to be mistaken for an island before dragging ships underwater.

items.title: The History of Mosaic Art
items.content_text: Mosaic art, made from small pieces of stone, glass, or tile, dates back over 4,000 years and spread across cultures from Mesopotamia to Byzantium.

items.title: Understanding Compassion Fatigue
items.content_text: Compassion fatigue is the emotional exhaustion that can affect people who repeatedly care for others in distress, common among caregivers and helpers.

items.title: Understanding the Barnum Effect
items.content_text: The Barnum effect describes why people rate vague, generic personality descriptions as highly accurate, believing they were written specifically for them.

items.title: What Causes Earthquakes?
items.content_text: Earthquakes happen when built-up stress along fault lines suddenly releases, sending seismic waves through the ground as tectonic plates shift.

items.title: What Is 5G and How Is It Different From 4G?
items.content_text: 5G is the fifth generation of mobile network technology, offering significantly faster speeds and lower latency than 4G through new radio frequencies.

items.title: What Is a Trade Deficit?
items.content_text: A trade deficit happens when a country imports more goods and services in value than it exports, and it isn't automatically a sign of economic weakness.

items.title: What Is a VPN and How Does It Work?
items.content_text: A VPN encrypts your internet traffic and routes it through a remote server, masking your real location and protecting your data on public networks.
